subject.title: Owner-signed responsibility gates for assistant memory, actions, skills, and evidence reuse

question: Should OpenClaw define an owner-confirmed durable memory/evidence lifecycle in native memory/plugin APIs, or leave this as plugin/ClawHub-level governance for now?
rationale: The issue asks for new policy, schema, config, UI, and security semantics across persistent memory, skill/action outputs, and reusable evidence; automation cannot choose that product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Design native responsibility contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the minimal durable states, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and review/revoke UX before implementation.

options.title: Scope to memory-core only
options.body: Limit the first design to memory promotion and retrieval, leaving skill/action/evidence governance for later plugin API work.

options.title: Defer to external governance plugins
options.body: Document SCBKR, UMP, or similar systems as external prior art and avoid native lifecycle changes until a concrete missing OpenClaw API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design native responsibility contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define the minimal durable states, plugin visibility, migration behavior, and review/revoke UX before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest current history across the memory-core and plugin hook contract surfaces this decision would touch.
